title: 闻一闻压干的书页  (Smelling the Pressed Page)

segments.t: Inside quiet Room Nine, Mei and Teacher Song hold the thirty-year-old stained recipe card and the open botanical book beside the sunny glass window. Listen first.
小美，把晕开的卡片朝下午的阳光斜一点——看清那半个字了吗？
两勺温……只剩左边一个虫字旁，水痕旁边还有个圆小画！
那颗长着三片尖树叶的小圆果实不是柠檬——是甜橙子！
等等——温的虫字旁加甜橙皮丝！那个字会不会是野花蜂蜜的蜂？！
好孩子，闻闻卡片夹了三十年的那一页书吧。
闭上眼睛深吸一口气：花园薄荷、甜橙皮，还有金色的蜂蜜！
没错！温蜂蜜又柔软又清亮，既不发酸，也不会硬成石头！
再撒一小撮甜橙皮丝，既提莓果的香味，又不会酸到老陈！
快看边角最后没晕开的几个字：上面撒烤香的薄杏仁片。
两勺温蜂蜜、甜橙皮丝，再加烤香的杏仁片！
三号盘在炉子架上还温着呢——大厨，快去刷吧！
宋老师，您坐在琴木凳上别动；真正的蛋糕五分钟就到！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小美，把晕开的卡片朝下午的阳光斜一点——看清那半个字了吗？

'Tilt the smudged card slightly toward the afternoon sun, Mei—can you make out that half character?' "Chao" angles an action "toward" the afternoon sun, and "kan qing" glues "look" to "clear" for "make out clearly".
两勺温……只剩左边一个虫字旁，水痕旁边还有个圆小画！

'Two spoons of warm... only an insect character-side remains on the left, with a tiny round sketch beside the stain!' Rain washed away the right side, leaving "chong zi pang"—the left "insect component" written inside Mandarin's word for bee.
那颗长着三片尖树叶的小圆果实不是柠檬——是甜橙子！

'That tiny round fruit growing three pointed leaves is not a lemon—it is a sweet orange!' Read "zhang" ("grow") rather than "chang" ("long"), "zhang zhe" shows the fruit sporting three flat leaves counted with "pian".
等等——温的虫字旁加甜橙皮丝！那个字会不会是野花蜂蜜的蜂？！

'Wait—that warm insect-side character plus shredded sweet orange peel! Could that character be the character bee from wildflower honey?!' Clue solved: "feng" ("bee") starts with that exact insect component on the left, forming "fengmi" ("bee-nectar", honey).
好孩子，闻闻卡片夹了三十年的那一页书吧。
'Smell the page right where the card rested for thirty years, my dear.' Teacher Song's gentle "hao haizi" literally literally means "good child"—a warm elder's way of saying "my dear".
闭上眼睛深吸一口气：花园薄荷、甜橙皮，还有金色的蜂蜜！

'Close your eyes and breathe in deeply: garden mint, sweet orange peel, and golden honey!' "Shen xi yi kou qi" literally says "deeply inhale one mouthful of air"—the vivid everyday phrase for taking a deep breath.
没错！温蜂蜜又柔软又清亮，既不发酸，也不会硬成石头！

'Of course! Warm honey stays soft and glossy—neither turning sour nor hardening into stone!' Balanced "ji bu... ye bu..." builds a clean "neither... nor..." pair, while "fa suan" literally means "turn sour".
再撒一小撮甜橙皮丝，既提莓果的香味，又不会酸到老陈！

'And a pinch of shredded sweet orange peel lifts the berry aroma without puckering Chen!' "Yi xiao cuo" counts a tiny pinch held between fingertips, and "chengpi si" literally names fine shreds of orange peel.
快看边角最后没晕开的几个字：上面撒烤香的薄杏仁片。

'Look at the last unsmudged words at the corner: scatter toasted thin almond flakes on top.' Everyday spoken Mandarin reads standalone "bao" for "thin", pairing it with "pian" ("flat slice/flake") for almond flakes.
两勺温蜂蜜、甜橙皮丝，再加烤香的杏仁片！
'Two spoons of warm honey, shredded sweet orange peel, plus toasted almond flakes!' "Zai jia" ("again add") is how home cooks tack on the final crowning touch to a recipe list.
三号盘在炉子架上还温着呢——大厨，快去刷吧！
'Tin Three is still staying warm on the stove rack—hurry and brush it now, Chef!' Putting "zhe ne" right after "wen" ("warm") keeps the state ongoing—"still sitting nice and warm right now!"
宋老师，您坐在琴木凳上别动；真正的蛋糕五分钟就到！

'Do not move from that wooden piano bench, Teacher Song; the real cake will arrive in five minutes!' Quick "jiu" in "wu fenzhong jiu dao" promises a tiny wait—"in just five minutes it will be right here!"
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Sunlight and a baker's keen nose unlock the thirty-year stain: warm honey, sweet orange peel, and toasted almond flakes! See you next time.
下次见！
